intro: Appliance repairers find and fix faults in customers' homes. The closest of the 25 careers below is small engine repair at an 84% match, while electric motor repairers are 79% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $56,210, or 10% more than the $50,990 appliance repairers earn.
why_it_works: A service call means finding the fault, explaining the cost and fixing it while the customer watches. O*NET rates repairing at 3.88 out of 5 for this job, and troubleshooting and equipment maintenance at 3.62. Motor, automotive and electronics repair use the same skills. About half of the matches need a certificate. The gaps are operation and control and negotiation.
tips: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers earn $109,910, which is 116% more, after an apprenticeship.
Boilermakers earn $76,410, or 50% more, and are a 73% match.
An HVAC or electrical certificate builds on your skills and opens larger systems work.

faq.q: What jobs can former appliance repairers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are small engine mechanics (84%), motor vehicle electronics installers (80%) and automotive service technicians (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. Automotive technicians earn $50,620, about 1% less than the $50,990 appliance repairer median, and use the same fault-finding approach on vehicles.

faq.q: Which careers for appliance repairers pay more?
faq.a: 15 of the 25 matches pay more. Elevator installers earn $109,910 (116% more), transportation equipment electricians $84,890 (66% more) and Boilermakers $76,410 (50% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Transportation equipment inspectors earn $92,100 for their broader group.

faq.q: Do appliance repairers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Often a certificate. 13 of the 25 matches need no more education than appliance repairers already have, including 6 of the top 10. A post-secondary certificate is common in close matches, held by 47% of workers in one of them.

faq.q: What skills should appliance repairers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, negotiation, systems evaluation and equipment maintenance. Operations monitoring already rates 3.5 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so larger systems and controls are the main steps toward better-paid trades.
